subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the domain of the real valued function f(x) = 1/log(2 − x).

mark_split.label: Conditions for the function to be defined

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this domain — the conditions the formula forces, and the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write both conditions
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks is for the conditions alone. Write every one of them down before solving any.
steps.memory_tip: log 1 = 0, so a logarithm in a denominator always removes the point where its input equals 1.
lines: The logarithm is in the denominator, so

recall.must_convey: That the input of the logarithm must be positive, giving x < 2, and that the logarithm itself may not be zero, which removes x = 1.
accept: two minus x greater than zero and log two minus x not equal to zero
log needs a positive input so x less than two and log is zero at input one so x is not one
the denominator is a logarithm so it cannot be zero which happens at x equals one
log denominator lo undi so zero kaakoodadu x equals one theeyali
x less than two but x not equal to one

steps.why: Two rules apply at once: the input of a logarithm must be positive, and a denominator may not be zero. log(2 − x) is zero exactly when 2 − x = 1, so x = 1 fails even though the logarithm is defined there.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 2 − x > 0 and forgetting that the logarithm sits in the denominator.

steps.label: Take out the single point
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the interval itself. Write it in interval form, and check every bracket.
steps.memory_tip: One interval with one point taken out of the middle, so the answer is two open pieces.
lines: Remove the single point x = 1 from it.

recall.must_convey: That the answer is minus infinity to 1, union 1 to 2, with both endpoints open.
accept: minus infinity to one union one to two
everything below two except the point one
two open intervals split at one
two kanna takkuva kaani one theeyali
x less than two and x not equal to one written as intervals

steps.why: The condition x < 2 gives one interval, and x ≠ 1 removes a single interior point, which splits that interval into two open pieces.
common_mistakes: Giving (−∞, 2) and losing the excluded point x = 1.
Removing x = 2 as well, although it is already outside the interval.
